name: Abd al-Rahim Mahmud
bio: Abd al-Rahim Mahmud was a Palestinian poet, born in 1331 AH (1913 CE) in Anabta, a village near Tulkarm; he studied there and at al-Najah College in Nablus, where Ibrahim Tuqan was among his teachers, and went on to teach Arabic at al-Najah. When the revolt against the British broke out in 1936 he fought in it, and when the British pursued him he went to Iraq, where he graduated from the military college in Baghdad as an officer, taught in Basra and took part in Rashid Ali al-Kaylani's revolt of 1941, before returning to teach at al-Najah. Al-Zirikli writes that one line still rang in his ears, from a poem Abd al-Rahim recited before Saud ibn Abd al-Aziz, then crown prince, on his visit to Palestine in 1935: “The Aqsa Mosque: have you come to visit it, or come to bid it farewell before it is lost?” When war came to Palestine in 1948 he joined the Arab Liberation Army as a lieutenant, and he was killed on 13 July 1948 (1367 AH) in the battle of al-Shajara near Nazareth, where he was buried. The poems that could be found were collected after his death in a diwan that has been printed several times.
